record.tranche_reason: The thesis reports its own width sweeps and measures of complexity and sharpness against generalization; these are conceptual tests of V2 and V7. Its Path-SGD comparisons do not test the optimizer claims as stated.
record.gate_note: The thesis also discusses and cites several original studies. Those cited results are not recorded as rows. The true-label versus random-label experiments report complexity measures, not held-out accuracy on random labels, so they do not test V1.
record.test_reason: The width sweeps directly measure V2 using one-hidden-layer ReLU networks and held-out error after fitting the training data. Figures 10.1–10.2 also contain comparisons relevant to V4 and V6 that the record overlooks.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The thesis argues that optimization-induced implicit regularization is central to generalization, develops complexity-based guarantees, finds that the tested measures do not explain every empirical pattern, and reports improved generalization from path-normalized optimization.
record.recipe_differences: The thesis directly repeats the hidden-width sweep associated with Neyshabur, Tomioka & Srebro, and adds censored-label and noisy-label settings. For V7 it uses the Keskar-style sharpness measure and its own comparisons rather than Jiang et al.'s magnitude-aware analysis.
record.method_sensitivity: The width trend is examined on MNIST, CIFAR-10, censored labels, and censored labels with 5 percent noise. In the sharpness experiments, results vary with the comparison: sharpness alone is insufficient across true/random labels, has poor behavior across global minima, and joint PAC-Bayes measures fail for wider networks.

fits_no_version.finding: Norm-based measures distinguish true-label and random-label VGG models, with larger differences as sample size increases.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Several complexity measures distinguish fitting natural labels from fitting random labels.

fits_no_version.finding: Fixed-radius Keskar sharpness inadequately distinguishes true/random-label models and global minima with different test errors; joint expected-sharpness/KL comparisons perform better in these settings.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sharpness and parameter scale jointly explain some comparisons that fixed-radius sharpness alone does not.

fits_no_version.finding: The joint PAC-Bayes measure improves through width 128 but fails to track continued generalization improvement in larger MNIST perceptrons.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The tested norm and PAC-Bayes measures do not explain every width-dependent generalization trend.

record.problems: Several key trends are presented only in figures without numeric values in the text. The sharpness comparisons use specific architectures, training setups and sharpness definitions; the thesis itself says the tested measures fail to explain some generalization behavior.
record.rows_left_out: No additional required result rows omitted. Complexity values comparing true and random labels are not assigned to V1 because they do not measure the held-out accuracy behavior named by that version.

untested.parts: The thesis reports fitting true and random labels, but does not report the required paired held-out accuracy comparison.
No controlled convolutional versus fully connected image-classification comparison.
Adam versus SGD, broader tuning, optimizer switching and decoupled weight decay are not tested. The relevant baseline comparison is AdaGrad versus SGD on image classifiers.
No batch-size sweep under controlled epoch budgets.
Very small training sets, excessive dropout, convolutional classifiers and joint removal of dropout and weight decay with augmentation are not tested.

The specified magnitude-aware tolerance measure, generalization-gap ranking against norm and margin measures, and CIFAR-10/SVHN comparison without augmentation are not established by these experiments.
No removal and retraining experiment using examples ranked by memorization.

missing.what: AdaGrad-versus-SGD training and test errors, separated by dataset, balanced initialization and dropout condition. AdaGrad is an adaptive optimizer covered by V4; excluding it merely because Adam is absent is incorrect. The supplied figure text does not identify curve values reliably enough for a directional verdict.

Matched test-error comparisons with versus without dropout, separately for each dataset and baseline optimizer. Networks use two 4000-unit hidden layers and retain units with probability 0.5. These comparisons test V6, but readable curve values are needed for condition-specific verdicts.
Unregularized width sweeps on the small natural-label MNIST and CIFAR-10 training sets, each containing 2000 examples. Existing rows cover only the censored and noisy conditions from this figure.

record.verdict_notes: The thesis is not a listed original-source identifier, so V2 verdicts are included. However, Chapter 4 overlaps the original Neyshabur–Tomioka–Srebro work, and Section 7.5 explicitly repeats its experiment; these are not independent replications. No V4 or V6 directional label is assigned because the supplied figure extraction does not reliably resolve the relevant baseline curves.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out accuracy comparison for natural versus random labels.
The thesis tests one-hidden-layer fully connected networks on MNIST and downsampled CIFAR-10; it does not test all stated architectures or settings.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
Path-SGD and AdaGrad comparisons do not test Adam versus SGD or the conditions in this version.
Dropout appears in other experiments, but the thesis does not test the dropout claims in this version.
The thesis tests Keskar-style sharpness and PAC-Bayes measures, but not Jiang et al.'s magnitude-aware ranking across the stated CIFAR-10 and SVHN settings.
